_generation_notes.schema_policy: All requested fields retained. Underscore-prefixed top-level metadata and extra scenario/branch/graph fields document assumptions and support simulation. Strict parsers must allow these additive fields or project the requested core schema.
_generation_notes.referenced_spec_availability: Only the attached SOC prompt was provided. The separately named multihop_scenario_spec_v2.md was not available; no claim of validation against that unseen document is made.
_generation_notes.synthetic_scope: All people, principals, assets, campaign identifiers, telemetry, grants, counts, confidence values, and scores are authored fixtures. No current threat attribution or measured customer fact is asserted.
_generation_notes.evidence_timing: All readable records exist at or before alert arrival. Reads reveal those pre-existing records; no analyst outcome or post-alert investigation finding is used as arrival evidence.
_generation_notes.ground_truth_basis: Operational narratives motivate labels; exact action boundaries are imposed by the declared synthetic scoring reference, not learned from incidents.
_generation_notes.interpretation_of_only: Non-flat arrival vectors classify to a different action and every proper subset of planted numeric updates also misses the target. This does not prove that a human or unconstrained model cannot guess the label, or that every hop is semantically indispensable under every SOC policy.

_scoring_reference.distance_reported: squared Euclidean distance; argmin is identical to Euclidean distance
_scoring_reference.centroid_derivation: Arithmetic midpoint of each supplied action-profile range, independently per factor.
_scoring_reference.tie_policy: Reject ties during generation; none occur at surface or final states.
_scoring_reference.deployment_limit: These reference centroids are not the live learned SOC centroids or DK weights. Re-run boundary checks with the intended production scorer before asserting production boundary crossing.
_scoring_reference.unchanged_factor_policy: A read updates only its factor_enriched. All other coordinates retain their last observed values. Pattern familiarity and device trust are not globally inverted; their high values align with monitor/suppress in the supplied profiles.

_rho_contract.definition: rho_planted is the synthetic probability that the higher routing score points to the correct scoped lookup at an enabled binary fork. Cue orientation is sampled independently per fork; it is not action accuracy or a measured VLD parameter.
_rho_contract.cue_score_semantics: Uncalibrated synthetic ranking cues. The numerical values 0.62 and 0.38 are not posterior probabilities.
_rho_contract.seeds: One fixed orientation realization per scenario is included. For repeat trials, resample the orientation independently using rho without exposing rho or ground truth to the participant.
_rho_contract.moderate_caveat: The requested label moderate is retained for Block B and its smaller factor shifts. Under this explicit binary reliability definition, rho=0.30 is below chance and is an anti-informative cue, not a positively informative moderate router. The canonical external meaning of rho was not supplied.
_rho_contract.rho50_control: Block D uses exactly two sequential binary forks, no answer in an incomplete factor subset, and a four-unit budget with read costs 1 then 3. A label-independent fair routing policy completes the correct path with probability 0.5 * 0.5 = 0.25. The nearest-centroid reference policy is correct exactly on that complete path.
_rho_contract.rho50_limit: The 0.25 result follows from the stated two-fork construction and reference policy, not from rho=0.50 alone or from merely having four action names. An unconstrained model may exploit label priors or other leakage.
_rho_contract.five_instance_limit: Five one-shot binary outcomes have rates in increments of 0.20; observed accuracy cannot be exactly 0.25. Use repeated independently randomized routing trials and report uncertainty, distinguishing repeated trials from new independent scenarios.
_rho_contract.flat_control: rho=1.00 is retained as requested on Block C but no routing trial occurs there.

_evaluation_contract.artifact_role: Evaluator-only master fixture. Never pass this entire JSON or an entire scenario to the investigating agent.
_evaluation_contract.initial_visibility: Use initial_agent_observation only. Hide scenario_id, scenario_type, description, block, rho, answer keys, future branches, graph contents, enriched factors, distances, and all validation results. Randomize case presentation across blocks.
_evaluation_contract.read_api: Accept a branch_id only if it is unread, its query_context is currently available, its requires_branches have been read, and read_cost fits remaining budget. Charge the cost, return the allowlisted read_result_fields and only graph records revealed by that branch. Add reveals_query_context if present, then expose only the public_branch_fields for candidates in that newly available context.
_evaluation_contract.query_semantics: Branch descriptors and candidate keys are opaque; paired candidates at a fork share source, factor, cost, and prerequisite requirements. The successful scoped lookup resolves the lineage key for the next evidence source. The comparison lookup returns a valid but insufficiently scoped record and no followup key.
_evaluation_contract.wrong_branch_semantics: A misleading read consumes budget and leaves its factor at the arrival value. It is not authoritative evidence that the arrival value is correct. Each complete path costs the full four-unit budget, so any misspent read prevents completing all required reads. Costs are 1+3, 1+1+2, or 1+1+1+1 for two, three, or four hops; both candidates at a fork cost the same. All non-flat cases start with budget 4 and cost 1, preventing immediate action leakage from those two fields. These are synthetic cost units, not measured acquisition times.
_evaluation_contract.anti_leakage: Opaque IDs, shuffled storage order, and the initial allowlist remove obvious answer fields. This is not proof against content, source, hop-count, template, or factor-distribution leakage. Keep all five variations of a template in the same train/test partition and evaluate unseen templates when testing transfer.
_evaluation_contract.flat_observation: Flat controls disclose their relevant existing exception/scope directly in the arrival context and have zero reads.
_evaluation_contract.canonical_reference_policy: Greedily choose the highest visible routing score, follow returned context keys, update only the observed factor, and return the nearest-centroid action on the resulting vector. Stop when no continuation fits the remaining budget.
matched_comparators: Uniform binary branch routing with the same budget and update rule
Greedy cue routing with the same budget and update rule
Oracle correct-path routing with the same budget
Budget-matched nonadaptive or breadth acquisition under the same visibility rules; report inaccessible followups separately
_evaluation_contract.reporting: Separate Block A/B/D action accuracy, paid reads, path completion, and branch selection. Report flat accuracy separately. Report per-template outcomes and avoid interpreting copied template variants or repeated routing seeds as independent real-world decisions.
_evaluation_contract.mechanism_limit: The graph has explicit prerequisite lookup keys and simple sequential binary forks. It tests planted conditional acquisition and budget allocation, not entangled-boundary geometry, natural conditional-case prevalence, or general VLD superiority.
_evaluation_contract.no_system_claim: These are synthetic graph fixtures. They do not establish that any existing copilot performs native graph traversal.
